title: Example — Create honors an explicit id
heroDesc: A tiny two-file change, shown as a worked example of the review.json shape. Read the capability, then the one high-risk card.
cap:
The new capability, in brief

POST /users now honors a client-supplied id instead of always minting one, so a caller can create a user with a known id.
callout:
Where to spend your attention. One question decides this change: is exposing a client-supplied id on the public create endpoint acceptable, or should it be constrained to the principal id?

Not shown here: the generated OpenAPI snapshot.

files.title: Create honors an explicit id (the 409 root cause)
files.why: The schema silently dropped a client-supplied `id`, so a second create attempt 409'd on email. The core already honored `input.id ?? randomUUID()`; this just exposes it, matching the documented `NewUser` contract.
points: Is exposing client-supplied `id` on the public create endpoint acceptable, or should it be constrained (e.g. only equal to the principal id)?
Needs a follow-up integration spec: "create honors an explicit id" (endpoint-coverage rule).
files.diffText:
diff --git a/src/http/schemas.ts b/src/http/schemas.ts
--- a/src/http/schemas.ts
+++ b/src/http/schemas.ts
@@ -37,6 +37,7 @@ import { z } from 'zod'
 export const NewUserSchema = z.object({
+  id: z.string().optional().openapi({ example: 'dev-admin' }),
   email: z.string().email(),
   displayName: z.string(),
 })

files.title: POST /users passes id through to the service
files.why: Threads the now-optional `id` from the validated body into `createUser`. Behavior is unchanged when `id` is absent.
points: Confirm the cast `input.id as UserId | undefined` is the only place the raw string becomes a branded id.
files.diffText:
diff --git a/src/http/router.ts b/src/http/router.ts
--- a/src/http/router.ts
+++ b/src/http/router.ts
@@ -64,7 +64,8 @@ app.openapi(createUserRoute, async (c) => {
-  return c.json(toDto(await userService.createUser(c.req.valid('json'))), 201)
+  const input = c.req.valid('json')
+  return c.json(toDto(await userService.createUser({ ...input, id: input.id as UserId | undefined })), 201)
 })
